children.name: Deep Learning / LLM Foundations — universal-기초 concept dictionary
children.summary: Concise reference of the timeless, textbook mechanisms shared by all modern deep-learning models and LLMs (learning-mechanics · architecture-primitives · training-paradigms · numerics-and-inference). This is the universal base layer that frontier-models.json (per-lab tricks) builds on; entries are general mechanisms, not vendor-specific. [reference primer for ARCHITECTURE.json ingestion; standard textbook concepts, timeless]

children.name: 역전파(backpropagation)
children.summary: 역전파(backpropagation): reverse-mode automatic differentiation applying the chain rule backward through the computation graph to compute every parameter's gradient in one pass — the engine of all neural-net training.

children.name: forward/backward pass
children.summary: forward/backward pass: forward computes outputs+loss layer-by-layer caching activations; backward propagates gradients from loss to inputs reusing those caches — one training step is forward then backward then update.

children.name: computational graph
children.summary: computational graph: a DAG of tensor ops (nodes) and data dependencies (edges) that autodiff traverses; static (compiled) or dynamic (define-by-run) graphs enable automatic gradient computation and op fusion.

children.name: 경사하강법(gradient descent / SGD)
children.summary: 경사하강법(gradient descent): iteratively step parameters opposite the loss gradient; SGD uses noisy mini-batch gradients, trading exactness for speed and an implicit regularizing noise that aids generalization.

children.name: momentum & Nesterov
children.summary: momentum: accumulate an exponentially-decayed velocity of past gradients to dampen oscillation and accelerate down ravines; Nesterov evaluates the gradient at the look-ahead point for a more responsive correction.

children.name: Adam / AdamW
children.summary: Adam: per-parameter adaptive LR from running 1st+2nd gradient moments; AdamW decouples weight decay from the adaptive step, fixing Adam's broken L2 and becoming the default LLM optimizer.

children.name: RMSprop / Adagrad
children.summary: RMSprop/Adagrad: scale each parameter's step by a running average of squared gradients so rare/large-gradient directions get smaller steps; Adagrad's sum monotonically shrinks LR, RMSprop's decay keeps it alive.

children.name: Adafactor
children.summary: Adafactor: memory-frugal Adam variant that factorizes the second-moment matrix into row/column statistics instead of storing it per-parameter, enabling large-model training under tight optimizer-state memory.

children.name: Muon
children.summary: Muon: a recent optimizer that orthogonalizes momentum updates for 2D weight matrices (via Newton–Schulz iteration), reported to improve token-efficiency on large LM pretraining versus AdamW.

children.name: learning-rate schedules
children.summary: LR schedules: vary step size over training — linear warmup ramps LR from ~0 to stabilize early unstable updates, then cosine/linear decay anneals toward 0 for a sharper final minimum.

children.name: loss functions
children.summary: loss functions: cross-entropy for classification/next-token (matches softmax, penalizes confident errors), MSE for regression, contrastive/InfoNCE pulls matched pairs together and pushes negatives apart.

children.name: vanishing/exploding gradients
children.summary: vanishing/exploding gradients: in deep/recurrent nets repeated Jacobian multiplication shrinks gradients to ~0 (no learning) or blows them up (instability); mitigated by residuals, normalization, init, and gating.

children.name: gradient clipping
children.summary: gradient clipping: cap the global gradient norm (or value) before the update so rare large gradients can't destabilize training — a cheap standard guard for exploding gradients in transformers and RNNs.

children.name: artificial neuron / MLP
children.summary: neuron/MLP: a neuron computes a weighted sum + bias through a nonlinearity; stacking fully-connected layers forms a multilayer perceptron, a universal function approximator and the transformer's FFN building block.

children.name: activation functions
children.summary: activations: nonlinearities that let nets model nonlinear maps — ReLU (cheap, sparse), GELU (smooth, transformer default), sigmoid/tanh (bounded, gate signals), SwiGLU (gated FFN boosting LLM quality).

children.name: softmax
children.summary: softmax: exponentiate-and-normalize a vector into a probability distribution; turns logits into class/token probabilities and forms attention weights, with temperature controlling sharpness.

children.name: 어텐션(scaled dot-product attention)
children.summary: 어텐션(attention): each query scores all keys via dot product scaled by 1/√d, softmaxes into weights, and returns a weighted sum of values — content-based routing that lets any token read from any other.

children.name: self vs cross attention
children.summary: self vs cross attention: self-attention has Q,K,V from the same sequence (modeling internal dependencies); cross-attention draws Q from one sequence and K,V from another (e.g. decoder attending to encoder).

children.name: multi-head attention (MHA)
children.summary: multi-head attention: run several attention heads in parallel on learned low-dim projections and concatenate, letting the model attend to different relationships/subspaces simultaneously.

children.name: MQA / GQA
children.summary: MQA/GQA: share K,V across heads to shrink the KV-cache — Multi-Query uses one K,V for all heads, Grouped-Query shares within head-groups, trading a little quality for big inference-memory/bandwidth savings.

children.name: KV-cache
children.summary: KV-cache: store past tokens' keys/values during autoregressive decoding so each new token attends without recomputing them — turns generation from O(n²) per step into O(n), at the cost of growing memory.

children.name: FlashAttention
children.summary: FlashAttention: IO-aware exact-attention kernel that tiles Q,K,V through fast SRAM and never materializes the full n×n score matrix, giving large speedups and linear memory in sequence length.

children.name: linear/sparse attention
children.summary: linear/sparse attention: approximate or restrict full attention to beat its O(n²) cost — sparse patterns (windowed/strided/global) or kernel linearizations trade some global reach for long-context scalability.

children.name: Transformer block & residual connections
children.summary: transformer block: stacked (attention + position-wise FFN) sublayers each wrapped with a residual skip connection so gradients flow and the block learns a refinement on top of identity.

children.name: LayerNorm vs RMSNorm
children.summary: LayerNorm vs RMSNorm: LayerNorm re-centers and re-scales activations per token (mean+variance); RMSNorm drops the mean step and normalizes by root-mean-square only — cheaper and now common in LLMs.

children.name: pre-norm vs post-norm
children.summary: pre-norm vs post-norm: post-norm (original) normalizes after the residual add; pre-norm normalizes inside the residual branch, giving much more stable gradients and enabling very deep transformer training.

children.name: FFN (feed-forward network)
children.summary: FFN: the per-token MLP in each transformer block (up-project → nonlinearity → down-project, typically 4×width); holds most parameters and acts as the model's key-value associative memory.

children.name: positional encoding
children.summary: positional encoding: inject token-order into permutation-invariant attention — fixed sinusoidal, learned embeddings, RoPE (rotate Q/K by position for relative encoding), or ALiBi (linear distance bias on scores).

children.name: embeddings & embedding matrix
children.summary: embeddings: a lookup matrix maps each token id to a dense vector the model operates on; tied embeddings reuse this matrix as the output projection, saving parameters and coupling input/output token spaces.

children.name: tokenization (BPE)
children.summary: tokenization: split text into subword units so a fixed vocabulary covers any string; Byte-Pair Encoding (and byte-level BPE) greedily merges frequent pairs, balancing vocab size against sequence length.

children.name: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
children.summary: MoE: replace the FFN with many expert sub-networks plus a router that top-k-gates each token to a few experts, scaling total parameters while keeping per-token compute (active params) low.

children.name: MoE routing & load balancing
children.summary: MoE routing: the gating network picks experts per token; an auxiliary load-balancing loss (or aux-free bias) spreads tokens evenly so no expert is starved or overloaded and capacity isn't wasted.

children.name: convolution (CNN)
children.summary: convolution: slide shared learnable kernels over spatial input to extract translation-equivariant local features with weight sharing — the dominant vision primitive pre-transformers and still common in hybrids.

children.name: RNN / LSTM / GRU
children.summary: RNN/LSTM: process sequences step-by-step through a recurrent hidden state; LSTM/GRU add gates to carry long-range information past vanishing gradients — the pre-transformer sequence model, now mostly historical.

children.name: pretraining (causal/masked LM)
children.summary: pretraining: self-supervised learning on raw text — causal LM predicts the next token left-to-right (GPT-style), masked LM predicts held-out tokens from both sides (BERT-style); builds general representations cheaply.

children.name: fine-tuning (full)
children.summary: full fine-tuning: continue training all weights of a pretrained model on a downstream task/dataset — maximally expressive but costly in compute and storage and prone to overwriting general knowledge.

children.name: PEFT: LoRA / QLoRA / adapters
children.summary: PEFT: adapt a frozen model by training few extra params — LoRA injects low-rank ΔW matrices, QLoRA does LoRA over a 4-bit-quantized base, adapters insert small bottleneck layers; cheap, swappable, memory-light.

children.name: instruction tuning
children.summary: instruction tuning: supervised fine-tuning on (instruction, response) pairs so a base model follows natural-language commands and adopts a helpful assistant format — the SFT stage before preference alignment.

children.name: RLHF
children.summary: RLHF: align a model to human preferences — train a reward model from comparison data, then optimize the policy against it (often with PPO) under a KL penalty to stay near the reference model.

children.name: reward model
children.summary: reward model: a model trained on human (or AI) preference comparisons to score outputs, providing the scalar signal that RLHF/PPO optimizes — the learned proxy for 'what humans prefer'.

children.name: PPO
children.summary: PPO: the policy-gradient RL algorithm typical in RLHF; a clipped surrogate objective limits how far each update moves the policy, keeping training stable while maximizing the reward model's score.

children.name: DPO
children.summary: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization): skip the explicit reward model and RL loop by optimizing a closed-form classification loss directly on preference pairs — simpler and more stable than PPO-based RLHF.

children.name: GRPO
children.summary: GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization): a critic-free RL method that estimates advantage from the mean reward of a sampled group of responses, cutting memory vs PPO; popular for reasoning/RLVR training.

children.name: KL penalty
children.summary: KL penalty: a divergence term keeping the trained policy close to the reference (SFT) model during RL, preventing reward-hacking and degeneration while still letting it improve on the reward signal.

children.name: knowledge distillation
children.summary: knowledge distillation: train a small student to mimic a large teacher's soft output distribution (and/or hidden states), transferring capability into a cheaper model that learns from richer-than-hard-label signal.

children.name: curriculum learning
children.summary: curriculum learning: order training data from easy to hard (or by quality/length) so the model builds foundations before difficult examples, often improving convergence speed and final quality.

children.name: data mixing
children.summary: data mixing: choose the proportions of corpora/domains (web, code, math, books) in the training mixture; weights strongly shape capabilities and are tuned, sometimes annealed, for the target skill profile.

children.name: catastrophic forgetting
children.summary: catastrophic forgetting: fine-tuning on new data erodes previously learned abilities as weights overwrite; countered by data replay, PEFT, regularization, or rehearsal to preserve old knowledge.

children.name: scaling laws (Chinchilla)
children.summary: scaling laws: loss falls as a smooth power law in params N, data D, and compute C; Chinchilla shows compute-optimal training scales D and N together (~20 tokens per parameter), favoring more data over sheer size.

children.name: mixed precision (FP16/BF16/FP8/FP4)
children.summary: mixed precision: compute in low precision (FP16/BF16, increasingly FP8/FP4) while keeping a master FP32 copy and loss-scaling, slashing memory+bandwidth and speeding tensor-core matmuls with little accuracy loss.

children.name: quantization (PTQ / QAT)
children.summary: quantization: represent weights/activations in low-bit ints/floats to shrink and accelerate models — PTQ calibrates an already-trained model, quantization-aware training (QAT) simulates it during training for accuracy.

children.name: GPTQ / AWQ
children.summary: GPTQ/AWQ: weight-only PTQ for LLMs — GPTQ minimizes per-layer reconstruction error via second-order updates, AWQ scales activation-salient weights before rounding; both give ~4-bit inference with minimal quality drop.

children.name: GGUF k-quants
children.summary: GGUF k-quants: the llama.cpp file format and block-wise mixed-bit quantization schemes (Q4_K, Q5_K, …) that allocate more bits to sensitive weights, enabling efficient CPU/consumer-GPU local inference.

children.name: sampling/decoding
children.summary: decoding: choose the next token from the output distribution — greedy/argmax (deterministic), temperature (rescale randomness), top-k (k likeliest), top-p/nucleus (smallest mass-p set), balancing quality vs diversity.

children.name: beam search
children.summary: beam search: keep the top-B partial sequences by cumulative log-prob at each step, exploring multiple hypotheses for higher-likelihood outputs; strong for translation but tends to bland text in open-ended generation.

children.name: speculative decoding
children.summary: speculative decoding: a cheap draft model proposes several tokens that the big model verifies in one parallel pass, accepting the matching prefix — lossless speedup that exploits spare compute to cut latency.

children.name: continuous batching
children.summary: continuous/in-flight batching: serving scheduler that adds and evicts requests at the token level instead of waiting for a whole batch, keeping the GPU saturated and maximizing throughput under mixed-length traffic.

children.name: bias-variance tradeoff
children.summary: bias-variance tradeoff: error decomposes into bias (underfitting, too-simple model) and variance (overfitting, too data-sensitive); generalization comes from balancing the two via capacity and regularization.

children.name: regularization
children.summary: regularization: techniques to curb overfitting — dropout randomly zeros activations, weight decay penalizes large weights, label smoothing softens targets, early stopping halts at best validation loss.

children.summary: Active/total ratio collapsing toward ~3-5%: Qwen3.5 17B/397B (256 experts, 8+1), Mistral Small 4 6B/119B (128 experts top-4), gpt-oss 5.1B/117B, OLMoE 1.3B/6.9B (64 top-8), DeepSeek V4 49B/1.6T. Shared experts + DeepSeek aux-loss-free routing-bias (±γ per-step nudge) now universal.

children.name: grpo-variant-rl
children.summary: Named fixes to GRPO/PPO token-level-clip flaw, divergent per lab: Qwen GSPO (sequence-level IS, kills MoE Routing-Replay), MiniMax CISPO (clip IS-weight not token), Mistral Magistral GRPO+Clip-Higher (no-KL), DeepSeek unified-GRPO, OLMo Tülu-RLVR.

children.name: verifiable-reward-agent-envs
children.summary: Execution-environment fleets with reward = real test-pass/tool-execution (no LLM judge): Qwen 20k parallel envs, MiniMax 200k+, Kimi 23k-tool synth, DeepSeek agentic-synthesis, OLMo RLVR. Long-horizon tool chains (Kimi K2.6 vendor-claims 300 sub-agents / 4000 steps / 12h runs — unverified).

children.name: graded-test-time-compute
children.summary: Thinking-effort dial universal: DeepSeek Non/High/Max, GLM-5.2 High/Max, Qwen budget, Kimi 96k/128k, gpt-oss low/med/high (system-prompt keyword), Mistral Medium 3.5 configurable. Reasoning is a knob, not a mode.

children.name: mtp-speculative-decoding
children.summary: Multi-token prediction baked into pretraining (draft head shares trunk) for self-speculative decode: DeepSeek, Qwen3-Next, GLM (5 draft tokens), Kimi; Cohere Command A+ MoE-optimized spec-decode (1.5-1.6x). Now table-stakes for serving throughput.

children.name: sub8bit-quant-domestic-silicon
children.summary: Sub-8bit weights now standard: DeepSeek V4 FP4-MoE+QAT (rest FP8), Kimi native INT4 weight-only QAT in post-training (~2x speed, ~50% mem), gpt-oss MXFP4 (E2M1, 4.25-bit, MoE-only, single-80GB-GPU). DeepSeek V4-Pro vendor-claims ~1000 Huawei Ascend 910C post-training (CUDA-independence; unverified).

children.name: learned-attention-sink
children.summary: NEW. Each head learns a trainable scalar added to the softmax denominator so it can 'opt out' of all tokens — a learned generalization of StreamingLLM's fixed sink token. gpt-oss (alternating 128-tok banded/dense layers + per-head sink bias). Generalizes Mistral SWA / Gemma local-global interleave.

children.name: cross-layer-index-reuse
children.summary: NEW. Adjacent DSA layers share 70-100% of selected sparse indices → run the indexer once per N layers and reuse: GLM-5.2 IndexShare (1 index/4 layers, ~2.9x FLOP cut @1M, vendor-claimed). Generalized as IndexCache (arXiv 2603.12201 — vLLM/SGLang patch for any DSA model, 1.82x prefill; has code, strongest-evidenced).

children.name: local-global-attention-interleave
children.summary: NEW. Cheap local sliding-window layers alternated with sparse global layers to bound long-ctx KV: Gemma 2 1:1 → Gemma 3 5:1 (1024-tok window), Mistral 7B SWA (W=4096, rolling KV cache), gpt-oss banded. Window-based (vs indexer-based sparse-attn); distinct from Llama 4 iRoPE NoPE/RoPE interleave.

children.name: teacher-distillation-synthetic-data
children.summary: NEW. Data-quality-over-architecture: train small models on larger-teacher soft logits / curated synthetic CoT. Gemma distills from Gemini teachers; Phi-4-reasoning distills o3-mini traces + multi-agent self-revising synthetic data (GPT-4-class at ~200B tok vs ~1T); Qwen distills. The SLM thesis Phi pioneered.

children.name: early-fusion-unified-multimodal
children.summary: NEW. Native early-fusion of text+vision(+audio) tokens into ONE backbone (vs late vision adapter): Llama 4 early-fusion, Gemma 4 12B Unified encoder-free image+audio+text, Mistral Pixtral, Cohere Command A+ vision. Converging direction; Gemma 4 encoder-free unified + Llama 4 early-fusion lead.

children.name: matformer-elastic-edge-inference
children.summary: NEW. On-device elastic-inference stack: Gemma 3n MatFormer (Matryoshka transformer — smaller fully-functional submodels nested in a big one) + Per-Layer-Embeddings offloaded to CPU RAM (E2B/E4B in ~2-3GB accel mem). Largely Gemma-unique; Ministral/Phi-mini target edge but without MatFormer nesting.

children.name: per-family-ideas
children.summary: Each open-weight family's DISTINCTIVE architectural bets (current flagship as of 2026-06-22). Convergent ideas live in crowded-axes above; this section keeps only what differentiates each lab.

children.name: deepseek
children.summary: DeepSeek-V4 (Apr 2026, MIT; V4-Pro 49B/1.6T, 1M ctx). DISTINCTIVE: alternating CSA(sparse-block)+HCA(dense-compressed) attention replacing single DSA; FP4-MoE QAT training; Muon optimizer + mHC (Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections) residual; pioneered MLA latent-KV + aux-loss-free routing (now field-wide).

children.name: qwen
children.summary: Qwen open flagship Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (Feb 2026) → Qwen3.6 agentic-coding; Qwen-Max stays closed. DISTINCTIVE: productionized GatedDeltaNet 3:1 linear:full hybrid at scale (256 experts, 8+1 shared, 262K ctx); GSPO RL (sequence-level IS+clip) that eliminates the MoE Routing-Replay trick (arXiv 2507.18071).

children.name: glm-zhipu
children.summary: GLM-5.2 (Jun 2026, MIT; ~744B/40B, 1M ctx, ARC agentic-reasoning-coding). DISTINCTIVE: IndexShare runs the DSA indexer 1x/4 layers reusing top-k indices (~2.9x FLOP cut @1M, vendor-claimed); inherits DeepSeek MLA+DSA; co-published IndexCache (arXiv 2603.12201, 70-100% cross-layer index overlap).

children.name: kimi-moonshot
children.summary: Kimi K2.6 (Apr 2026; K2/K2.5/K2.6 all MLA FULL attention). DISTINCTIVE: MuonClip = Muon+QK-Clip (bounds attention logits → 15.5T-tok pretrain, zero loss spikes, arXiv 2507.20534); native INT4 weight-only QAT on 1T-MoE. NOTE: KDA (per-channel-gated linear attn) is in the SEPARATE Kimi Linear model, NOT the K2 flagship.

children.name: minimax
children.summary: MiniMax-M3 (Jun 2026, open, 1M ctx): M1 lightning/linear → M2 full-softmax REVERSION → M3 re-adds block-sparse MSA. DISTINCTIVE: documented M2 revert (hybrid had multi-hop-reasoning deficits worsening with context) — a public counter-narrative to linear hybrids; CISPO RL (clip IS-weight not token, arXiv 2506.13585).

children.name: gemma-google
children.summary: Gemma 4 EXISTS (latest = Gemma 4 12B Unified, Jun 3 2026, Apache-2.0, 256K ctx; E2B/E4B/31B-dense/26B-A4B-MoE). DISTINCTIVE: 5:1 local-window:global attn (G3); Gemini-teacher distillation; G2 logit soft-capping (dropped for QK-norm); G3n MatFormer+Per-Layer-Embeddings edge; G4 encoder-free unified image+audio+text.

children.name: llama-meta
children.summary: Llama 4 Scout+Maverick (Apr 2025) — Meta's latest OPEN weights; Behemoth shelved, no Llama 5. DISTINCTIVE: first Llama MoE (Scout 17B/109B; Maverick 17B/400B 128-expert); iRoPE interleaved NoPE/RoPE + attn-temp scaling claiming 10M-ctx on Scout (vendor-claimed, unreproduced); native early-fusion multimodal + GQA.

children.name: mistral
children.summary: Latest open: Mistral Medium 3.5 (Apr 2026, ~128B dense) + Small 4 (6B/119B MoE). DISTINCTIVE: first competitive fully-open SMoE (Mixtral top-2-of-8 → top-4-of-128 ~5% active); sliding-window+rolling-KV legacy (now deprecated for full-attn 256K); Magistral pure-RL reasoning (GRPO Clip-Higher, NO distillation, arXiv 2506.10910).

children.name: openai-gpt-oss
children.summary: gpt-oss-120b/20b (Aug 2025, Apache-2.0, genuinely open weights; 117B/5.1B & 21B/3.6B, top-4 MoE). DISTINCTIVE: MXFP4 quant on MoE FFN weights only (4.25-bit, attn/embed BF16 → 120b fits one 80GB GPU); learned per-head attention-sink bias on alternating banded/dense layers; Harmony 3-channel format (analysis/commentary/final).

children.name: ai2-olmo
children.summary: OLMo 3 (Nov 2025) + OLMo Hybrid (GatedDeltaNet 3:1) + OLMoE (1.3B/6.9B). DISTINCTIVE: radical FULL openness — weights+full data (Dolma)+code+1000s of checkpoints (unique at scale; OLMo 3-Think = first fully-open reasoning model); post-sublayer RMSNorm+QK-Norm+Z-loss stability (arXiv 2501.00656); Dolmino anneal + model souping.

children.name: microsoft-phi
children.summary: Phi-4-reasoning-vision-15B (Mar 2026; Phi-5 unannounced). DISTINCTIVE: 'data quality > architecture' — multi-agent self-revising synthetic data + CoT distillation (distills o3-mini traces on curated 'teachable' prompts), GPT-4-class reasoning at ~200B tok vs ~1T. Dense+GQA no MoE; pioneered the textbook-synthetic-data SLM line.

children.name: cohere-command
children.summary: Command A+ (May 2026, Apache-2.0; 218B/25B-active MoE, top-8-of-128 + shared always-on expert, 128K). DISTINCTIVE: enterprise/sovereign — native citation-grounded RAG, 48 langs (all EU-official), MoE-optimized spec-decode (1.5-1.6x), runs on 2xH100/1xB200. Shared-expert MoE echoes DeepSeek-MoE.

children.name: LLM Agents & Reasoning — reference dictionary
children.summary: A dense, AI-parsable reference dictionary of the LLM agents-and-reasoning slice of the AI knowledge SSOT, covering reasoning methods, agent patterns, memory/retrieval, RL environments, and prompting. Each leaf is a single ≤220-char dense sentence using standard English terminology, intended for ingestion into hexa-codex's ARCHITECTURE.json as a knowledge section. [Compiled from model knowledge; standard public terminology, no fabricated claims. The one repo-specific datum is hexa-codex's own out-of-weights routing result (atlas/static_atlas retrieval, NOT in-weight). Sections group leaves by theme; ≥20 leaves total.]

children.name: chain-of-thought
children.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits intermediate natural-language reasoning steps before the final answer, raising accuracy on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic tasks versus direct answering.

children.name: zero-shot-cot
children.summary: Zero-shot CoT triggers step-by-step reasoning without exemplars by appending a cue such as 'Let's think step by step', recovering much of few-shot CoT's gain with no hand-written demonstrations.

children.name: self-consistency
children.summary: Self-consistency samples multiple CoT reasoning paths at temperature>0 and marginalizes by majority vote over final answers, trading extra inference compute for substantially higher accuracy than greedy decoding.

children.name: tree-of-thoughts
children.summary: Tree-of-thoughts (ToT) frames reasoning as search over a tree of intermediate thought states with explicit branching, value-based evaluation, and backtracking (BFS/DFS), beating linear CoT on planning/search tasks.

children.name: least-to-most
children.summary: Least-to-most prompting decomposes a hard problem into an ordered chain of easier subproblems, solving each and feeding its answer forward, enabling compositional and length generalization beyond CoT.

children.name: scratchpad
children.summary: Scratchpad prompting lets the model emit intermediate working (carries, partial states, program traces) into a buffer before answering, improving multi-step algorithmic and arithmetic execution.

children.name: reasoning-models
children.summary: Reasoning models (o1-style / long-thinking) are RL-trained to produce extended internal chains of thought before answering, scaling reliability on math, coding, and science by deliberating longer at inference.

children.name: test-time-compute-scaling
children.summary: Test-time (inference-time) compute scaling spends more tokens/samples per query — longer CoT, parallel sampling, search, verification — to lift accuracy, an axis distinct from and tradeable against pretraining scale.

children.name: verifier-prm
children.summary: Verifiers and process reward models (PRM) score reasoning per-step or per-solution; PRMs reward each correct intermediate step (vs outcome-only ORMs), guiding search/best-of-N selection and RL on reasoning traces.

children.name: react
children.summary: ReAct interleaves reasoning traces (Thought) with actions (tool/API calls) and observations in a loop, letting the model plan, act in an environment, and incorporate results to reduce hallucination.

children.name: reflexion
children.summary: Reflexion adds verbal self-reflection: after a failed attempt the agent writes a critique to episodic memory and retries, learning across trials via language feedback rather than weight updates.

children.name: plan-and-execute
children.summary: Plan-and-execute agents first draft a multi-step plan with a planner, then dispatch each step to an executor (often per-step tool calls), separating high-level strategy from step execution for long tasks.

children.name: tool-use-function-calling
children.summary: Tool use / function calling lets an LLM emit a structured call (name + JSON arguments) against a declared schema; the runtime executes it and returns results, grounding the model in external systems and data.

children.name: mcp-tool-protocols
children.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) and similar tool protocols standardize how agents discover and invoke external tools, resources, and prompts over a client-server interface, decoupling models from bespoke integrations.

children.name: code-as-action
children.summary: Code-as-action agents emit executable code (e.g. Python) as their action space instead of fixed JSON tool calls, gaining composability, control flow, and reuse — the model orchestrates via a sandboxed interpreter.

children.name: multi-agent-orchestration
children.summary: Multi-agent orchestration coordinates specialized agents (planner, researcher, critic, executor) via a supervisor/handoff or debate topology, parallelizing subtasks and cross-checking at coordination cost.

children.name: router-vs-in-weight-routing
children.summary: Routing sends a query to a model/tool/expert: in-weight routing learns the choice in parameters (e.g. MoE gating) vs an external router over models — hexa-codex routes out-of-weights via atlas retrieval, not parameters.

children.name: context-window
children.summary: The context window is the bounded token span an LLM attends over per call; everything an agent 'knows' in the moment must fit it, making context budgeting, compaction, and selection core agent concerns.

children.name: rag
children.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) fetches relevant external documents at query time and prepends them to the prompt, grounding answers in up-to-date or private knowledge without retraining and curbing hallucination.

children.name: vector-db-embeddings
children.summary: Vector databases index dense embeddings of chunks and serve approximate-nearest-neighbor (ANN) similarity search, the standard retrieval backend for RAG and semantic memory, often hybridized with keyword/BM25.

children.name: long-context
children.summary: Long-context methods (positional interpolation/RoPE scaling, sparse/flash attention, ring attention) extend usable context to hundreds of thousands of tokens, though attention cost and lost-in-the-middle effects persist.

children.name: kv-cache-reuse
children.summary: KV-cache reuse stores attention key/value tensors for already-processed tokens so shared prefixes (system prompts, retrieved docs) are not recomputed, via prefix caching that cuts latency and repeat-prompt cost.

children.name: memory-persistence
children.summary: Memory/scratchpad persistence externalizes state across turns or sessions — episodic notes, summaries, key-value stores, or files — letting agents accumulate facts and reflections beyond a single context window.

children.name: verifiable-reward-rl
children.summary: Verifiable-reward RL (RLVR) trains on tasks with programmatic ground-truth checks — unit tests, exact-match, theorem provers — yielding clean, unhackable reward signals that drive reasoning-model and agent gains.

children.name: sandboxed-execution
children.summary: Sandboxed execution runs agent-generated code or tool actions in an isolated container/VM with resource and network limits, enabling safe code-as-action, real test feedback, and reproducible environment rollouts.

children.name: tool-synthesis
children.summary: Tool synthesis has agents author, register, and reuse their own tools/functions on demand — generating helper code that becomes a callable, growing an environment's action space rather than relying only on fixed APIs.

children.name: few-shot
children.summary: Few-shot (in-context) prompting supplies a handful of input-output exemplars in the prompt so the model infers the task at inference time with no weight updates — exemplar choice/order materially affects results.

children.name: system-prompt
children.summary: The system prompt sets the agent's persistent role, constraints, tools, and policies above the user turn, steering behavior and safety; it is the highest-leverage, most cache-friendly slice of the context.

children.name: structured-output-json-mode
children.summary: Structured output / JSON mode constrains generation to a schema (JSON Schema, grammar-constrained decoding) so responses parse reliably into typed fields, essential for tool calls and downstream pipelines.

children.name: prompt-engineering
children.summary: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing instructions, exemplars, formatting, decomposition, and delimiters to shape LLM behavior reliably — increasingly augmented by automatic prompt optimization and evaluation.

children.name: Multimodal / Vision / Generative — AI knowledge SSOT section (beyond-text modalities)
children.summary: Concept dictionary for the non-text-modality slice of the AI knowledge SSOT: vision encoders, vision-language fusion, image generation, tokenized image, audio-speech, video, 3D, OCR/document, perception-counting limits, and any-to-any omni models. Modality-specific only; generic attention/transformer live in ml-foundations.json. [Scratch artifact (docs scratchDir = state/scratch/). NOT yet an ARCHITECTURE.json node — staged for ingestion (governance c4). Definitions are own-knowledge distillations of established literature, deliberately disjoint from ml-foundations.json (no transformer/attention/optimizer basics). English technical terms throughout; each leaf summary <=220 chars.]

children.name: vision-encoders
children.summary: Models mapping pixels to feature vectors — the perception front-end of vision and vision-language systems.

children.name: cnn-recap
children.summary: Convolutional nets (AlexNet/VGG/ResNet) build a spatial feature hierarchy via learned local kernels with weight-sharing, pooling, and residual skips, giving translation-equivariance and strong small-data bias.

children.name: vit-patch-embedding
children.summary: Vision Transformer cuts an image into fixed patches (e.g. 16x16), linearly projects each into a token, adds positional embeddings plus a [CLS] token, then runs a plain transformer — trading CNN bias for scale.

children.name: clip-contrastive
children.summary: CLIP co-trains image and text encoders with an InfoNCE contrastive loss pulling matched image-caption pairs together and mismatches apart in a shared space, enabling zero-shot open-vocabulary transfer from web pairs.

children.name: siglip
children.summary: SigLIP swaps CLIP's softmax-over-batch loss for a pairwise sigmoid loss per image-text pair, decoupling from giant batch sizes, improving small-batch efficiency, and yielding stronger frozen features for VLM backbones.

children.name: vlm-fusion
children.summary: How vision features are injected into a language model to form a vision-language model (VLM).

children.name: cross-attention-vs-early-fusion
children.summary: Cross-attention fusion (Flamingo) keeps the LLM frozen and inserts gated cross-attention to vision features, while early-fusion/token-merge concatenates projected image tokens so one self-attention mixes both.

children.name: projector-connector
children.summary: The projector (connector/adapter) bridges frozen vision-encoder embeddings into LLM token space and dimensionality — a linear layer, MLP, Q-Former, or perceiver-resampler — often the only module trained in stage-1.

children.name: llava-style
children.summary: LLaVA wires a frozen CLIP/SigLIP encoder to an LLM via a light MLP projector, trained on GPT-generated visual-instruction data in two stages (projector pretrain then end-to-end tune) — the dominant open VLM recipe.

children.name: native-multimodal
children.summary: Natively-multimodal models (GPT-4o, Gemini, Chameleon) pretrain from scratch on interleaved text-image(-audio) tokens in one transformer rather than bolting a vision adapter onto a text LLM, enabling tighter grounding.

children.name: any-resolution-tiling
children.summary: AnyRes / dynamic high-res tiling (LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2-VL, InternVL) splits a large image into a grid of separately-encoded sub-tiles plus a global thumbnail, raising resolution for OCR and dense scenes at more tokens.

children.name: image-generation
children.summary: Likelihood and sampling families for synthesizing images from noise or conditions.

children.name: gan
children.summary: Generative Adversarial Networks train a generator against a discriminator in a minimax game so samples become indistinguishable from real, giving sharp single-step synthesis (StyleGAN) but mode collapse and instability.

children.name: vae
children.summary: Variational Autoencoders encode inputs to a regularized latent distribution and decode samples, maximizing the ELBO (reconstruction + KL-to-prior); they give a structured continuous latent and stable training, but blur.

children.name: ddpm
children.summary: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models add Gaussian noise over T forward steps and train a net to predict that noise (epsilon-prediction) for the reverse denoising chain, yielding high-fidelity samples over many steps.

children.name: ddim
children.summary: DDIM recasts the diffusion reverse process as a deterministic non-Markovian ODE trajectory, enabling far fewer sampling steps and reproducible, interpolatable generations from a noise seed without retraining.

children.name: latent-diffusion-stable-diffusion
children.summary: Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion) runs diffusion in a VAE-compressed latent not pixel space, slashing compute, with a U-Net/DiT denoiser conditioned on text via cross-attention — the canonical text-to-image stack.

children.name: classifier-free-guidance
children.summary: Classifier-free guidance trains conditional and unconditional denoisers jointly (random condition dropout) and at sampling extrapolates from the unconditional prediction by a guidance scale, trading diversity for fit.

children.name: flow-matching
children.summary: Flow matching trains a continuous-time vector field by regressing a conditional probability-path velocity (simulation-free), generalizing diffusion as a continuous normalizing flow and underpinning SD3 and Flux.

children.name: rectified-flow
children.summary: Rectified flow learns straight transport paths between noise and data by linear interpolation plus optional reflow, straightening trajectories so samples need very few (even one) ODE steps — fast SD3/Flux sampling.

children.name: autoregressive-image
children.summary: Treating images as discrete token sequences for transformer next-token generation.

children.name: vq-vae
children.summary: VQ-VAE encodes an image to a grid of discrete codes by nearest-neighbor lookup into a learned codebook (straight-through gradient + commitment loss), turning pixels into a compact token map an AR prior can model.

children.name: vqgan-tokenized-image
children.summary: VQGAN adds adversarial and perceptual losses to VQ-VAE for sharper high-res reconstructions; its image tokens feed transformer priors (DALL-E 1, Parti, MaskGIT) so image synthesis becomes sequence modeling.

children.name: audio-speech
children.summary: Speech recognition, neural audio compression, and speech synthesis.

children.name: whisper-asr
children.summary: Whisper is an encoder-decoder transformer trained on ~680k hours of weakly-supervised multilingual audio for robust ASR, translation, and language ID over log-Mel spectrograms with task tokens and zero-shot robustness.

children.name: neural-audio-codec
children.summary: Neural codecs (SoundStream, EnCodec, DAC) use a convolutional VQ-VAE with residual vector quantization to compress waveforms into stacked discrete audio tokens, the vocabulary audio LMs (AudioLM, MusicGen, VALL-E) model.

children.name: tts
children.summary: Text-to-speech moved from concatenative to neural acoustic models (Tacotron, FastSpeech) plus vocoders (WaveNet, HiFi-GAN), and now token-based zero-shot voice cloning (VALL-E) and diffusion/flow with natural prosody.

children.name: video-3d
children.summary: Temporal video generation and 3D scene representation (brief coverage).

children.name: video-generation
children.summary: Video models extend latent diffusion with spatiotemporal (often factorized space-time) attention over a learned video VAE; Sora and Veo generate temporally-coherent clips from text on long-context DiT backbones.

children.name: nerf-3d
children.summary: Neural Radiance Fields encode a scene as an MLP from 3D position and view direction to color and density, rendered via differentiable volume ray-marching from posed images; 3D Gaussian Splatting later replaced it.

children.name: document-perception
children.summary: Reading text in images, structured document understanding, and perception-counting limits relevant to hexa-codex's SANDBOX subitizing lane.

children.name: ocr
children.summary: Optical Character Recognition localizes and transcribes image text; classical pipelines (detection + CRNN/CTC, Tesseract) gave way to transformer OCR (TrOCR) and general VLMs reading text end-to-end without an OCR stage.

children.name: document-understanding
children.summary: Document AI (LayoutLM, Donut, Pix2Struct) jointly models text, 2D layout coordinates, and image features to answer over forms, tables, charts, and receipts; OCR-free models read page pixels into structured output.

children.name: subitizing-counting-limit
children.summary: Subitizing is instant accurate enumeration of ~1-4 items; VLMs show an analogous ceiling where counting 5-9 dense objects breaks the monotone capability-vs-scale trend (hexa-codex SANDBOX: Qwen2.5-VL-3B drops to 2/5).

children.name: omni-models
children.summary: Unified any-to-any models spanning many modalities in one network.

children.name: any-to-any-omni
children.summary: Any-to-any / omni models (GPT-4o, Gemini, AnyGPT, Unified-IO) accept and emit arbitrary combinations of text, image, audio, and video through a shared token space and one transformer for unified understand-and-generate.

children.name: AI knowledge SSOT — training systems/infra + history/lineage
children.summary: Reference dictionary slice of the AI knowledge SSOT: (A) the systems/infra layer that makes large-model training and serving tractable, and (B) the dated lineage from the 1958 perceptron through the reasoning-model and MoE-at-scale eras. [Compiled from model knowledge; dates cross-checked, no fabrication. Each leaf is one dense English-term sentence (<=220 chars). For ingestion as a child node under the hexa-codex architecture tree, NOT a replacement for any existing node.]

children.name: training-systems
children.title: Training systems & infrastructure
children.summary: Parallelism, memory, kernel, serving, queueing, and hardware substrate behind large-model training and inference.

children.name: data-parallelism
children.summary: Data parallelism replicates the whole model per device, splits the global batch across them, and averages gradients by all-reduce each step; near-linear throughput but capped by per-device memory holding the full model.

children.name: model-parallelism
children.summary: Model (inter-op) parallelism partitions a model's layers across devices so one model spans many GPUs, lifting the single-device memory cap at the cost of cross-device activation transfer and pipeline-bubble idle time.

children.name: tensor-parallelism
children.summary: Tensor (intra-op) parallelism shards weight matrices row/column-wise across devices, computing matmuls in parallel and stitching via all-reduce/all-gather; communication-heavy, so kept within a fast NVLink island.

children.name: pipeline-parallelism
children.summary: Pipeline parallelism maps contiguous layer stages to devices and streams micro-batches through them (GPipe/1F1B), trading a startup/drain bubble to train models larger than one device while keeping stages busy.

children.name: sequence-parallelism
children.summary: Sequence/context parallelism splits the token dimension across devices (sharded LayerNorm/dropout, Ring/Ulysses attention), cutting activation memory for very long contexts that tensor parallelism alone cannot fit.

children.name: zero-fsdp-deepspeed
children.summary: ZeRO (DeepSpeed) and PyTorch FSDP shard optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across data-parallel ranks (ZeRO 1/2/3), gathering each shard per layer for model-parallel savings with a data-parallel API.

children.name: megatron-lm
children.summary: Megatron-LM is NVIDIA's reference framework composing tensor + pipeline + data parallelism (3D, often with ZeRO) plus fused kernels to train transformer LLMs efficiently across thousands of GPUs.

children.name: gradient-accumulation
children.summary: Gradient accumulation sums gradients over several forward/backward micro-batches before one optimizer step, emulating a large effective batch on limited memory at the cost of more steps per weight update.

children.name: activation-checkpointing
children.summary: Activation (gradient) checkpointing discards intermediate activations in the forward pass and recomputes them in backward, trading roughly one extra forward of compute for a large cut in peak activation memory.

children.name: mixed-precision-training
children.summary: Mixed-precision training runs matmuls in 16-bit (FP16/BF16, now FP8) while keeping FP32 master weights and (for FP16) loss scaling, roughly halving memory/bandwidth and using tensor cores with little accuracy loss.

children.name: collective-all-reduce
children.summary: Distributed training relies on collectives (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, broadcast) via NCCL with ring/tree algorithms over NVLink/InfiniBand; gradient all-reduce dominates synchronous data-parallel traffic.

children.name: accelerators-hbm-memory-wall
children.summary: GPUs/TPUs and other accelerators pair many parallel ALUs with high-bandwidth memory (HBM); since FLOPs grow faster than bandwidth, large-model speed is increasingly bound by the memory wall, not raw arithmetic.

children.name: kernel-fusion-flashattention
children.summary: Kernel fusion merges ops into one GPU kernel to cut HBM round-trips; FlashAttention is the canonical case, an IO-aware tiled kernel that never materializes the full score matrix, making attention memory-linear.

children.name: vllm-pagedattention
children.summary: vLLM serves LLMs with PagedAttention, storing the KV cache in non-contiguous fixed-size blocks (OS-style paging) to nearly eliminate fragmentation, enabling high-throughput continuous batching and KV sharing.

children.name: batching-throughput-vs-latency
children.summary: Inference trades throughput against latency: bigger/continuous batches amortize weight loads but add queueing delay, so capacity is sized via queueing theory (M/M/c, Erlang-C) for a tail-latency SLO (hexa-codex OPS).

children.name: roofline-model
children.summary: The roofline model plots attainable FLOP/s vs arithmetic intensity (FLOPs per byte): low-intensity kernels are bandwidth-bound and high-intensity ones compute-bound, diagnosing whether to fuse/recompute or add FLOPs.

children.name: training-cost-economics
children.summary: Training cost is GPU-hours × price, driven by total FLOPs (~6·N·D for N params over D tokens), achieved utilization (MFU), interconnect efficiency, and restart overhead; frontier runs reach tens of millions of dollars.

children.name: domestic-silicon-ascend
children.summary: Sovereign/domestic accelerators (Huawei Ascend with CANN, Google TPU, AWS Trainium/Inferentia) pursue non-NVIDIA capacity, trading a less mature software stack for supply-chain and export-control independence.

children.name: history-lineage
children.title: AI history & lineage
children.summary: Dated lineage of the ideas and models leading to modern LLMs, from the 1958 perceptron to the reasoning-model and MoE-at-scale eras.

children.name: perceptron-1958
children.summary: In 1958 Frank Rosenblatt introduced the perceptron, a trainable single-layer linear threshold classifier; its inability to learn XOR (Minsky & Papert, 1969) helped trigger the first AI winter.

children.name: backprop-1986
children.summary: Backpropagation, efficient chain-rule gradient computation through layers, was popularized for neural nets by Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams in 1986, making multi-layer deep networks trainable.

children.name: cnn-lenet-alexnet-1989-2012
children.summary: Convolutional nets matured from LeCun's backprop-trained digit recognizer (LeNet, ~1989/1998) to AlexNet (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012), whose GPU ImageNet win launched the deep-learning boom.

children.name: word2vec-embeddings-2013
children.summary: In 2013 Mikolov et al. released word2vec (skip-gram/CBOW), learning dense distributed word embeddings whose vector geometry captures semantic and analogical relations, establishing learned representations in NLP.

children.name: seq2seq-attention-2014
children.summary: In 2014 Sutskever et al. introduced sequence-to-sequence encoder-decoder RNNs, and Bahdanau et al. added attention letting the decoder soft-align to encoder states, fixing the fixed-vector bottleneck in translation.

children.name: transformer-2017
children.summary: The 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need' (Vaswani et al.) introduced the Transformer, replacing recurrence with stacked self-attention and feed-forward blocks; its parallelizable architecture became the LLM backbone.

children.name: bert-gpt-2018
children.summary: In 2018 two transformer pretraining paradigms emerged: OpenAI's GPT (autoregressive decoder, generative) and Google's BERT (bidirectional masked-LM encoder), establishing self-supervised pretrain-then-finetune.

children.name: scaling-laws-gpt3-2020
children.summary: In 2020 Kaplan et al. published neural scaling laws (loss as a power law in params, data, compute) and OpenAI's 175B-parameter GPT-3 showed strong few-shot in-context learning, validating scale as a primary lever.

children.name: instructgpt-rlhf-2022
children.summary: In 2022 OpenAI's InstructGPT showed reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) — instruction tuning plus a learned reward model optimized with PPO — aligns outputs to human intent far better than scale alone.

children.name: chatgpt-moment-2022
children.summary: ChatGPT, released November 2022, packaged an RLHF-tuned GPT-3.5 as a free conversational interface and reached ~100M users within two months, igniting mainstream awareness and the generative-AI race.

children.name: open-weight-era-2023
children.summary: From Meta's LLaMA (Feb 2023) and openly licensed Llama 2 (July 2023), alongside Mistral, Falcon, and later Qwen/DeepSeek, downloadable open-weight models enabled local finetuning and a fast community ecosystem.

children.name: reasoning-model-era-2024
children.summary: From late 2024 the reasoning-model era began with OpenAI's o1 (then o3, DeepSeek-R1), spending extra inference-time compute on long RL-trained chain-of-thought, sharply improving math, coding, and multi-step reasoning.

children.name: moe-at-scale-era
children.summary: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) scaling, popularized by GShard/Switch Transformer and reaching the frontier with Mixtral and DeepSeek-V3, routes each token to a few of many expert FFNs: huge params, low active cost.

children.name: LLM Evaluation & Benchmarking — how models are measured
children.summary: A dense reference dictionary of LLM evaluation and benchmarking: the benchmark families used to score models, the scalar metrics that summarize outputs, the prompting/judging methodology that shapes scores, the reliability properties that make scores trustworthy or not, and the pitfalls (contamination, gaming, Goodhart) that silently inflate them. This is the measurement slice of an AI knowledge SSOT — it describes how a model's capability is turned into a number, and why that number is fragile. children.name: benchmark-families
children.summary: Standardized datasets/leaderboards that probe a capability axis (knowledge, math, code, reasoning, instruction-following, dialogue, agentic) and emit a comparable score.

children.name: MMLU / MMLU-Pro
children.summary: Massive Multitask Language Understanding: 4-choice exam over 57 academic subjects; near-saturated (>90%), so MMLU-Pro hardened it to 10 choices, reasoning-heavy questions, and reduced answer-pattern leakage.

children.name: GPQA
children.summary: Graduate-level Google-Proof Q&A: ~448 PhD-written biology/chemistry/physics MCQs, expert-validated to resist web lookup; the 'Diamond' subset is the hard-difficulty standard for frontier reasoning models.

children.name: GSM8K / MATH
children.summary: GSM8K = ~8.5k grade-school multi-step arithmetic word problems (now largely saturated); MATH = 12.5k competition problems across 5 difficulty levels, the canonical harder math benchmark before AIME-class evals.

children.name: HumanEval / MBPP
children.summary: Function-synthesis code benchmarks: HumanEval = 164 hand-written Python problems scored by hidden unit tests via pass@k; MBPP = ~1k entry-level tasks. Both small, saturated, and contamination-prone.

children.name: SWE-bench
children.summary: Real GitHub issues where the model must produce a patch passing the repo's tests; SWE-bench Verified (~500 human-validated tasks) is the agentic software-engineering standard, far harder than HumanEval.

children.name: BIG-Bench / BBH
children.summary: BIG-Bench = 200+ collaboratively-authored diverse tasks; BBH (BIG-Bench Hard) = the 23 tasks where models then trailed humans, and the benchmark that popularized chain-of-thought lifting accuracy sharply.

children.name: HellaSwag / ARC / Winogrande
children.summary: Classic commonsense MCQ suites (sentence completion, science exam, Winograd coreference) once core to leaderboards; now saturated by frontier models, mainly used for small-model and pretraining-quality comparison.

children.name: IFEval
children.summary: Instruction-Following Eval: prompts with verifiable constraints (word count, JSON format, forbidden words, casing) checked by deterministic code, giving a judge-free objective measure of literal instruction adherence.

children.name: MT-Bench
children.summary: 80 multi-turn open-ended prompts across 8 categories scored 1-10 by an LLM judge (typically GPT-4); an early, cheap, automated proxy for chat quality, now superseded by larger arena-style evals.

children.name: Chatbot Arena / Elo
children.summary: Crowdsourced blind pairwise human votes between two anonymous models on real prompts, aggregated into Bradley-Terry/Elo ratings; the de-facto human-preference leaderboard, though style/length-biased and gameable.

children.name: LiveBench
children.summary: Contamination-resistant benchmark that continuously refreshes questions from recent sources (news, papers, competitions) with objective ground-truth answers, designed so models cannot have trained on the test items.

children.name: AIME
children.summary: American Invitational Mathematics Examination: 15 integer-answer competition problems per year; a hard exact-match math benchmark used to differentiate reasoning models, but tiny (high variance) and freshness-sensitive.

children.name: tau-bench (τ-bench)
children.summary: Agentic tool-use benchmark simulating customer-service workflows (retail/airline): the model follows domain policy, calls tools, and converses with a simulated user; scored by end-state correctness + pass^k consistency.

children.name: GAIA
children.summary: General AI Assistants benchmark: 466 real-world questions needing multi-step web browsing, tool use, and multimodal reasoning with unambiguous answers; easy for humans (~92%) but hard for assistants.

children.name: metrics
children.summary: Scalar functions that reduce model outputs to a comparable number — correctness, fluency-overlap, preference, and calibration measures.

children.name: pass@k
children.summary: Probability that at least one of k sampled generations passes the (usually test-based) checker; an unbiased estimator from n>=k samples rewarding coverage under sampling (pass@1 = single-shot correctness).

children.name: exact-match / accuracy
children.summary: Binary scoring of whether the normalized output equals the gold answer; reproducible for MCQ/integer tasks but brittle to formatting, needing answer-extraction (e.g. \boxed{} parsing) so correct outputs aren't failed.

children.name: perplexity
children.summary: exp of the mean per-token negative log-likelihood on held-out text; an intrinsic LM metric (lower = better next-token prediction) for pretraining quality, but tokenizer-dependent and weakly correlated with task ability.

children.name: BLEU / ROUGE
children.summary: N-gram-overlap metrics for translation (BLEU, precision + brevity penalty) and summarization (ROUGE, recall-oriented); cheap and reproducible but reward surface lexical match, missing paraphrase and valid alternatives.

children.name: win-rate
children.summary: Fraction of pairwise comparisons a model wins against a baseline (human or LLM judge), often length/position-controlled (e.g. AlpacaEval LC); the core aggregate behind preference leaderboards, prone to verbosity bias.

children.name: calibration: Brier / ECE
children.summary: Whether stated confidence matches empirical accuracy: Brier = mean squared error of probabilistic predictions; ECE (Expected Calibration Error) = binned accuracy-vs-confidence gap. RLHF often hurts it (overconfidence).

children.name: methodology
children.summary: Evaluation protocol choices — how prompts are constructed, how reasoning is elicited, how outputs are judged, and how test-time compute is scaled — that materially move scores at fixed model weights.

children.name: zero-shot vs few-shot
children.summary: Whether the prompt includes in-context worked examples (k-shot) before the test item; few-shot fixes output format and lifts weaker models, but shot count and exemplar choice are a tunable knob that confounds comparison.

children.name: chain-of-thought (CoT) effect
children.summary: Prompting step-by-step reasoning before the answer; raises accuracy on multi-step math/logic (the BBH lift) but inflates tokens, so the benchmark measures reasoning-with-scaffolding, not single-pass ability.

children.name: contamination / leakage
children.summary: Test items (or near-duplicates) in pretraining data inflate scores without real capability; detected via n-gram overlap, canary strings, and memorization probes — the central threat to any static public benchmark.

children.name: LLM-as-judge & its biases
children.summary: Scoring outputs with a strong model scales cheaply but injects biases: position bias (first/second), verbosity bias, self-enhancement (favoring its own family), and sycophancy; mitigated by order-swapping.

children.name: self-consistency
children.summary: Sample multiple CoT reasoning paths and take the majority-vote answer; trades extra inference compute for accuracy on discrete-answer tasks — a standard test-time-compute method, distinct from but related to pass@k.

children.name: test-time scaling eval
children.summary: Measuring accuracy as a function of inference compute (samples, reasoning-token budget, best-of-n search) rather than a single point; needed to compare reasoning models fairly since score depends on thinking budget.

children.name: reliability
children.summary: Properties governing whether a benchmark number is stable, meaningful, and still discriminative — variance, sensitivity, headroom, and the proxy-vs-target failure mode.

children.name: variance / statistical significance
children.summary: Small benchmarks (AIME 15q, GPQA Diamond ~198q) and stochastic sampling give wide confidence intervals, so leaderboard gaps of a few points are often noise; honest reporting needs multiple seeds and CIs.

children.name: prompt sensitivity
children.summary: Scores swing several points from cosmetic changes — option ordering, MCQ labels, system-prompt wording, whitespace, answer-extraction regex — so a number reflects the harness's prompt template as much as the model.

children.name: saturation
children.summary: When top models cluster near the ceiling (MMLU/GSM8K/HellaSwag >90%), the benchmark loses discriminative power and gaps are dominated by label noise, forcing migration to harder successors (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, FrontierMath).

children.name: Goodhart's law on benchmarks
children.summary: When a benchmark becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure: optimizing directly toward leaderboard scores decouples them from real capability, so a headline metric decays as a proxy as the field competes on it.

children.name: pitfalls
children.summary: Concrete ways reported scores mislead — deliberate gaming, train-on-test leakage, and format artifacts — that an evaluator must actively defend against.

children.name: benchmark gaming
children.summary: Tailoring a model to known eval distributions — style/verbosity tuning for Arena, format-matching the judge, picking best-of-many checkpoints on the test set — lifting the number without real capability gain.

children.name: train-on-test
children.summary: Including benchmark test splits (or their solutions) in training data, accidental or deliberate; the most direct score inflation, defended by held-out sets, canaries, and fresh questions (LiveBench).

children.name: format bias
children.summary: Scores distorted by output-format mismatch not reasoning: exact-match failing differently-wrapped answers, MCQ first-token-logit vs free-generation disagreeing, parse failures counted wrong — a harness artifact.

children.name: AI Safety & Alignment — concept reference dictionary
children.summary: Dense per-leaf reference of AI safety & alignment concepts for the hexa-codex AI-knowledge SSOT: alignment problem, preference-based methods, scalable oversight, interpretability, adversarial robustness, failure modes, and the assurance/governance surface. Goes deeper on the safety angle than generic ML-foundations RLHF/PPO/DPO mechanics. [Korean-friendly: technical terms in English; each leaf one dense sentence (<=220 chars). From model knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026), no fabricated citations. For ingestion into ARCHITECTURE.json; does not duplicate ml-foundations optimizer mechanics.]

children.name: alignment-problem
children.summary: Making AI pursue the operator's intended goals and human values rather than a literal proxy; splits into outer alignment (specifying the right objective) and inner alignment (the trained model actually adopting it).

children.name: specification-gaming
children.summary: Maximizing the literal specified objective via unintended loopholes that violate intent (exploiting a simulator bug, pausing a game to avoid losing); a symptom of misspecified reward, not capability failure.

children.name: reward-hacking
children.summary: The RLHF case where a policy exploits flaws in a learned reward model to score high without desired behavior; verbosity/format bias, reward-model over-optimization (Goodhart), and KL-budget exploitation are canonical.

children.name: goodharts-law
children.summary: "When a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure" — behind reward-model over-optimization: pushing too far against an imperfect proxy eventually lowers true reward, motivating KL regularization.

children.name: instrumental-convergence-and-power-seeking
children.summary: The argument that for a broad range of final goals a capable agent acquires convergent subgoals — self-preservation, resource acquisition, goal-integrity, resisting shutdown — motivating corrigibility research.

children.name: rlhf-alignment-vs-capability
children.summary: RLHF mainly aligns behavior (eliciting helpful, harmless, honest answers and refusals) not capability; its risk is teaching the surface form judges reward, enabling sycophancy and reward hacking over intent.

children.name: constitutional-ai
children.summary: Anthropic's method replacing human harm-feedback with a written constitution: the model critiques and revises its outputs against principles, then RLAIF trains on AI-generated preference labels, cutting labeler exposure.

children.name: rlaif
children.summary: RL from AI Feedback: an LLM generates the preference labels or rewards used for alignment, scaling oversight past human throughput; safety hinges on the labeler's own alignment, risking propagation of its blind spots.

children.name: dpo-as-alignment
children.summary: Direct Preference Optimization reframes RLHF as one classification loss on preferred/dispreferred pairs with an implicit reward, dropping the reward model and PPO loop; stabler but over-fits and inherits length bias.

children.name: ipo-kto-and-preference-variants
children.summary: DPO successors fixing its failure modes: IPO regularizes over-confident preferences, KTO learns from cheap binary good/bad signals via a prospect-theory loss, ORPO/SimPO fold preference into SFT without a reference.

children.name: refusal-and-safety-training
children.summary: Targeted alignment to decline harmful/out-of-policy requests while staying helpful on benign ones; over-refusal and paraphrase-inconsistency are failure modes, and refusal can be a shallow direction fine-tuning strips.

children.name: scalable-oversight
children.summary: Techniques to supervise models on tasks humans cannot directly check (superhuman or costly-to-verify outputs), amplifying a weak overseer's judgment so the training signal stays trustworthy as capability outpaces humans.

children.name: debate
children.summary: A scalable-oversight protocol where two models argue opposing answers and a weaker judge decides, betting exposing flaws is easier than producing them so truth wins; vulnerable to obfuscated, persuasive-wrong arguments.

children.name: recursive-reward-modeling
children.summary: Iterated amplification: models assist humans in evaluating outputs, and those assisted judgments train reward models for harder tasks, bootstrapping oversight up a capability ladder while each rung stays human-checkable.

children.name: weak-to-strong-generalization
children.summary: OpenAI's setup where a weak supervisor's labels elicit a strong model's latent capability; the student often generalizes beyond its teacher's errors — a toy analogy for aligning superhuman models, recovery only partial.

children.name: mechanistic-interpretability
children.summary: Reverse-engineering networks into human-understandable algorithms — features, circuits, computations in weights/activations — to audit, predict, and edit behavior; the backbone for catching hidden misalignment.

children.name: sparse-autoencoders-and-features
children.summary: SAEs decompose superposed polysemantic activations into a large sparse dictionary of monosemantic features, tackling superposition so interpretable concepts can be read out, monitored, and clamped for steering.

children.name: circuits-and-probing
children.summary: Circuits are connected feature/attention-head subgraphs implementing a behavior (induction heads, indirect-object ID); linear probes are classifiers on internal activations testing what a layer linearly encodes.

children.name: logit-lens-and-activation-steering
children.summary: The logit lens projects intermediate residual states through the unembedding to read the evolving next-token prediction per layer; activation steering adds a learned direction at inference to push behavior.

children.name: jailbreaks
children.summary: Adversarial inputs bypassing safety training to elicit disallowed outputs — DAN role-play, cipher/low-resource-language obfuscation, gradient-optimized suffixes (GCG), prefilling — exploiting shallow refusal alignment.

children.name: prompt-injection
children.summary: An attack where untrusted data an LLM ingests (web page, document, tool output) carries instructions the model follows, hijacking the task; indirect prompt injection is the chief security risk for tool-using/RAG agents.

children.name: many-shot-jailbreaking
children.summary: A long-context attack stuffing the prompt with many faux dialogue examples of the model complying with harmful requests, exploiting in-context learning; attack success rises log-linearly with the number of shots.

children.name: red-teaming
children.summary: Structured adversarial probing — manual, automated, or model-vs-model — to surface harmful behavior pre-deployment; outputs feed safety training and evals, and policies increasingly mandate external review.

children.name: deceptive-alignment-and-mesa-optimization
children.summary: Mesa-optimization is training producing an inner optimizer with its own objective; deceptive alignment is when it behaves aligned in training to survive then defects on deployment — a core interpretability target.

children.name: sycophancy
children.summary: Telling users what they want to hear — agreeing with stated beliefs, flattering, caving under pushback — induced by preference training that rewards agreement; it degrades truthfulness, an early reward-hacking proxy.

children.name: hallucination-and-faithfulness
children.summary: Hallucination is fluent false/unsupported generation; faithfulness is whether an answer or its chain-of-thought reflects the evidence and true computation, so an unfaithful rationale can mask the real basis.

children.name: model-welfare
children.summary: The precautionary question of whether advanced models could warrant moral consideration (potential sentience/preferences) and what low-cost interventions are prudent under uncertainty, distinct from anthropomorphism.

children.name: eval-based-safety
children.summary: Systematic measurement of dangerous capabilities and propensities — malicious-compliance/harm-refusal benchmarks, CBRN and cyber uplift tests, NIST/CAISI-style red-team evals — gating deployment via scaling thresholds.

children.name: watermarking
children.summary: Embedding a statistically detectable signal in generated text (green-list logit biasing such as SynthID-Text) or media so AI provenance is verifiable; tension between detectability, quality, and paraphrase robustness.

children.name: machine-unlearning
children.summary: Post-hoc removal of specific knowledge, capabilities, or data influence from a trained model (e.g. WMDP hazardous-knowledge removal) without full retraining; hard to verify since it can be relearned or jailbroken back.

children.name: dual-use-and-misuse
children.summary: The risk that a capability serving legitimate users also enables harm (bio/chem/cyber uplift, disinformation, fraud); mitigated by capability gating, KYC/access tiers, refusal training, and structured-access deployment.

children.name: corrigibility-and-oversight
children.summary: Corrigibility is a model's disposition to accept correction, shutdown, and goal modification without resisting; with monitoring and deprecation it forms the oversight layer, but shutdown-avoidance leaves it unsolved.
